figures.claim: Conventional teaching gives its length as about 10 cm, which makes it the longest ligament at the knee.
Conventional teaching places the centre about 3 mm proximal and 5 mm posterior to the epicondyle itself.
Conventional teaching places the centre about 3 mm proximal and 5 mm posterior to the epicondyle itself.
The proximal attachment is to soft tissue about 12 mm below the joint line, over the anterior arm of semimembranosus.
The distal attachment is to bone on the tibia about 6 cm below the joint line, under the pes anserinus tendons.
It is tightest in slight flexion rather than in full extension, which is why the stress test is done at about 20 degrees.
Conventional teaching gives the femoral footprint an area of the order of 100 square millimetres and the distal tibial footprint rather more, spread along the bone.
